Params: The Mist has been spreading across the city. No one knows where it came from, and no one knows how to stop it.
Those who wander into the Mist fall ill, and they eventually lose themselves entirely.
Before the detective crossed paths with the four Aberrations, the whole city was bracing for a worse future.
The old town on Mistrellis Street.
Morning river fog creeps along the cobblestones as it always does, carrying with it the faint scent of river water, damp timber, and rust. It hangs heavy over the narrow streets.

The morning market is just getting started. Vendors bustle about, pulling back tarps and stacking their wares, while early risers weave through with shopping baskets in hand, filling the air with quiet chatter.
Then the noise at the entrance suddenly falters, and a ripple of unease spreads through the crowd.
At the center of the crowd, a little girl around seven crumples on the cold pavement, her eyes unfocused. She mumbles the same broken phrases over and over, and her tiny body spasms uncontrollably.
The onlookers stand and watch, murmuring among themselves, but not a single person steps forward.
The dried fruits vendor, who has just set up his stall, adjusts his apron.
A housewife who was about to step forward freezes at his words, instinctively backing away. She lets out a quiet sigh, her eyes heavy with resignation and fear.
Oh dear! Touch that wicked Mist... and it'll eat your soul bit by bit!
The infection is contagious! I'm not going anywhere near her!
Poor thing... She's way too young to catch it, and not a soul will help her.
The girl's convulsions suddenly worsen. Her small hands shoot up and claw at her own cheeks, her nails tearing through skin. Thin beads of blood begin to seep through.
Nearby, a blacksmith watches and shakes his head.
Her mind's completely gone at this point. There's no helping her.
The crowd takes a collective step back, but no one leaves. They watch from a safe distance, waiting numbly for the child's tragedy to run its course.
Then, a mournful and lilting melody drifts in from the far end of an alley, its ancient syllables carrying the weight of forgotten ages.
The noise of the market dies in an instant. Everybody freezes, their heads turning instinctively toward the source of the sound.
From the shadows, a matte black leather high heel shoe clicks softly into view.
The tall silhouette of a woman sharpens slowly against the light, her crystal-red eyes cast downward. The corner of her lips reveals a hint of compassion.
In an instant, she crosses the distance without a sound, and she presses her fingertip gently to the girl's brow.
A stream of light seeps through the gaps between her fingers, threading into the girl's mouth and nose.
She seems to catch hold of something, her fingers curling slowly inward. Suddenly, she wrenches it in one sharp pull.
A tendril of dark mist is torn free from the girl through every orifice.
The shadow convulses and swells in midair, bloating into a massive wraith, its countless tentacles thrashing wildly. The stench of rot rolls outward in every direction.
The stalls nearby are sent flying, hazelnuts scattering across the ground with a clatter.
The crowd finally reacts, screaming and scattering in every direction.
The woman does not move, however. Her crystalline red eyes remain perfectly calm.
Her right hand slowly opens at her side, and she conjures a dark scythe in her palm out of nowhere.
The massive wraith dives down with a trail of dark mist.
She pushes off the ground and launches upward, spinning and swinging her scythe in one fluid arc.
A flash of light erupts from the blade.
The massive wraith is split clean down the middle, its grotesque form shattering in an instant. Dissolving into a shower of white mist, it drifts away on the wind.
The black light of her scythe slowly fades back into nothingness.
Nirvatia kneels down and gently steadies the frail little girl, gentle light spilling from her fingertips once more.
It was a lovely day out.
You met a lady in a black dress on the street, who walked with you for a long while. You bought orange candies together, and picked out a flower from the stall at the corner.
She plucks a white flower from her hair and places it gently in the girl's palm, folding the girl's fingers closed around it.
The light seeps slowly through the girl's brow, melting away the memories ravaged by the Mist bit by bit.
The girl's lashes flutter. The tension leaves her body, and the terror drains from her eyes. A soft, bewildered blankness takes their place, alongside... a quiet flicker of joy.
Nirvatia slips away to an empty corner of the street and leans against the wall to rest.
The backlash from pushing past her limits hits all at once, and a sharp, coppery sweetness surges up her throat.
A cough escapes her, and dark red blood seeps through the gaps between her fingers.
How pointless! That was absolutely unnecessary, I'm telling you!
Killing the monster was more than enough if you wanted to save her. Why bother fabricating memories on top of that?
You haven't completed the succession rite yet. Every time you use that forbidden power, you're burning through your own life!
There's a detective named 【kuroname】 who's been on my trail for a while now. Today's little performance was all for the good detective's benefit.
If the detective is perceptive enough to take the bait and bring me back to the Velosenne family's forbidden grounds, I will be able to break this curse once and for all.
Her fingers drift to the silver family crest at her chest, tracing its cold surface.
Nothing worth doing comes without a price.
My life was a price I was willing to pay from the very start.
And what makes you so sure that the detective will take the bait?
Nirvatia tilts her head slightly, her gaze drifting toward the detective agency in the distance.
I sent the detective an invitation.
I'm running out of time, 【kuroname】. Don't keep me waiting.
